Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.

The parent brick is then approximated with a new rank-reduced Tucker decomposition [S1].

The claim states that the parent brick is approximated with a new rank-reduced Tucker decomposition [S1]. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states: 'Each octree brick A ∈ R3 is tensor approximated using rankreduced Tucker decomposition.' It further details that for each brick of size B^3, a rank-(R, R, R) TA (Tucker Approximation) is computed. Since 'parent brick' refers to a non-leaf brick in the octree hierarchy described, and the text confirms that every brick (including those constructed from children, i.e., parents) undergoes this approximation process, the claim is fully supported by the evidence.

Higher $K$ values increase reconstruction time and detail [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that 'Higher K values add more details onto the dataset.' Regarding reconstruction time, the text notes that 'Reconstruction steps occur only upon GPU cache misses' and that 'Lower-rank reductions give a faster outline.' By logical inference, since lower ranks (lower K) result in faster processing (faster outline), higher ranks (higher K) involve more computation, thereby increasing reconstruction time. Thus, the claim that higher K values increase both reconstruction time and detail is supported by the text.
